clue.text: Pay for alcohol producer making complete lack of progress

parts.note: to stand someone a drink is to pay for it
a still is the apparatus that distils spirits

explanation.surface: A distillery owner covers the bill while business grinds to a halt.
explanation.definitionFit: A halt where nothing moves is the idiom for a total absence of progress.

clue.text: Security for instance covering most of fair

indicators.note: the first word's letters wrap round the second piece like a cover

parts.note: say is used to introduce an example, like 'for instance'

indicators.note: only most of the word is used, its final letter dropped

parts.note: a fete is a fair, often a village one

explanation.surface: Someone cites fairground protection measures as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Safety and security are synonyms, both meaning protection from harm.

clue.text: Likely to keep book on rugby short

indicators.note: the first word holds the following pieces inside it

parts.note: apt to do something means likely to do it
RU stands for Rugby Union

explanation.surface: A book about rugby is probably going to be brief.
explanation.definitionFit: Short and brusque in manner are synonyms of curt or sudden.

clue.text: Considers touts floundering in such retail outlets

indicators.note: floundering means struggling clumsily, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A shop owner weighs up the ticket touts flailing around in bargain shops.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans back on the rest of the clue: such outlets as the anagram describes.
explanation.definitionFit: Shops selling goods at reduced prices are retail outlets of a cheap kind.

clue.text: Best of the bunch becoming boss

definitions.meaning: the pick of a bunch, here a pun on a bunch of fruit

explanation.surface: The finest of a group gets promoted to leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for the most important person, and literally the finest fruit in a hand of them.

clue.text: Meditative position of many outside university

indicators.note: the first piece sits outside, around the second

parts.note: lots means many

explanation.surface: Many students meditate on the lawn outside the university.
explanation.definitionFit: The cross-legged seated pose used in yoga and meditation.

clue.text: Parody, but avoid dismissing Queen

indicators.note: dismissing means sending away, so a letter is removed

parts.note: to skirt an issue is to avoid it
R, for Regina, stands for a queen

explanation.surface: A satirist mocks but steers clear of sacking the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A short comic sketch sending something up is a kind of parody.

clue.text: Eager to finish early with mistress, collapse

indicators.note: the word stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: keen means eager
a mistress is a lover

explanation.surface: An eager man leaves early with his mistress and then faints.
explanation.definitionFit: To topple over or faint is to collapse, like a boat capsizing.

clue.text: Trials covering English politician creating storms

indicators.note: the first word wraps around the following pieces

parts.note: tests are trials
MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician

explanation.surface: Scandal coverage about an English MP stirs up storms.
explanation.definitionFit: Violent weather events with high winds are also called storms or gales.

clue.text: Coy nurse is worried with bank's way of ending letter!

indicators.note: worried means agitated, so the letters are shaken up

parts.note: to bank on something is to rely on it; the 's links

explanation.surface: A shy nurse frets over how her bank signs off its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional formal valediction placed before the signature.

clue.text: Develops classes

explanation.definitionFit: A verb meaning takes shape, and a noun for British school year groups.

clue.text: Crude, favourite part one plays with little hesitation

parts.note: a pet is a favourite
a role is a part an actor plays
um is a small hesitant noise

explanation.surface: An actor hesitates slightly over a favourite but rough part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crude' looks like an adjective; it is the noun for unrefined oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude is unrefined oil straight from the well.

clue.text: Snack keeping Olympic chiefs sweet

indicators.note: the first word holds the second inside it

parts.note: a tapa is a Spanish snack
the IOC, International Olympic Committee, runs the Games

explanation.surface: Olympic bosses are offered nibbles and dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: A pudding made from cassava pearls, a classic British school dessert.

clue.text: Mean character's goose cooked with credit being restricted

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking the definition

indicators.note: the credit piece is confined inside the rearranged letters
cooked suggests the letters are altered or fiddled

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: A miser cooks the Christmas goose while short of credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' sounds culinary beside the goose but signals the anagram, giving SOOGE; 'being restricted' confines the credit abbreviation within.
explanation.definitionFit: The miserly figure from Dickens's A Christmas Carol, a byword for stinginess.

clue.text: Of historic South American extraction, getting very heated

parts.note: Incan means of the Inca empire of old Peru
extraction means ancestry, descent

explanation.surface: Someone of Inca ancestry gets furious.
explanation.definitionFit: Glowing white-hot, and figuratively seething with fury.

clue.text: Committed theologian importing repackaged iced tea

indicators.note: importing means bringing in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a theologian

indicators.note: repackaged means put together anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A devout scholar brings in bottled iced tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repackaged' turns ICED TEA into EDICATE, which goes between the D and D.
explanation.definitionFit: Devoted and wholly given to a cause are synonyms.

clue.text: Brought out priest alluded to

parts.note: Eli is the Old Testament priest who taught Samuel
cited means referred to

explanation.surface: A cleric is drawn out and mentioned.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw a response or fact from someone is to evoke or extract it.

clue.text: Daring, popular, cool — about right!

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: tepid means lukewarm, cool

explanation.surface: A fearless, trendy and laid-back person is spot on.
explanation.definitionFit: Fearless and bold are synonyms of brave.

clue.text: Well-established pine substitute burning at last

parts.note: to pine for is to long for
a stand-in is a substitute

indicators.note: takes only the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A pine replacement finally catches fire in the old forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pine' looks like a tree; it is the verb meaning yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: Existing for a long time and firmly rooted, as with a tradition.

clue.text: Doctor appears in put-up travel document as writer

indicators.note: the doctor shows up inside the other piece
in a down clue put up means written bottom to top

parts.note: a visa is a travel document
MO, Medical Officer, is a doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor features in a raised passport stamp for an author.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'put-up' means read upwards, so the document is written bottom to top before the doctor goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Asimov was a prolific science fiction author.

clue.text: Pastry with filling of hard deposit

parts.note: a tart is a pastry

indicators.note: the filling is the inside, so the middle letters are taken

explanation.surface: A pastry with a rock-hard filling leaves a residue.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard crust that builds up on teeth is a deposit, as is that in wine casks.

clue.text: Drivers sharing complain, ladies perhaps being rejected

parts.note: to carp is to complain

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the ladies is one example of a loo, a toilet

explanation.surface: Commuters grumble when the women's toilets are turned away.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrangement in which several motorists take turns giving lifts.

clue.text: Bug found in popular vaporiser

indicators.note: the letters are discovered inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: An insect turns up in a trendy vape.
explanation.definitionFit: An insect grub in its immature stage, loosely a bug.

clue.text: Club style of boots

explanation.definitionFit: A London football club, and elastic-sided ankle boots named after the district.

clue.text: Protest planned about European Commission is not to be disclosed

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters surround the next piece
planned means arranged, so the letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: A demonstration against Brussels is kept quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'planned' signals the anagram, giving TOPSRET, and 'about' wraps those letters round the Brussels abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Classified at the highest level, so confidential and hidden.

clue.text: The setter turned and encountered a tourist

indicators.note: turned means flipped round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me
met means encountered

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler spun round and bumped into a holidaymaker.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cornwall an emmet (literally ant) is a disparaging word for a tourist.
explanation.definitionFit: Cornish dialect for a visitor, from the old word for an ant.

clue.text: Swell expected to swamp east of Ireland

indicators.note: swamping means engulfing, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: due means expected

indicators.note: the east end of an across word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A big wave is forecast to flood Ireland's east coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swell' looks like a wave; it is the old noun for a dandy.
explanation.definitionFit: A dandy or smart man about town is a swell in old slang.

clue.text: View oddly depicted in heraldry, redesigned rarely

indicators.note: redesigned means drawn up anew, so the letters are rearranged
oddly takes the odd-numbered letters of the word

explanation.surface: A view seldom appears in a coat of arms that has been redrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' gives VE, the first and third letters of View, which join HERALDRY in the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Almost never and seldom are synonyms of infrequently.
